Calculate vectorial capacity reduction for a list of interventions

Source: R/model_impact.R
calculate_impact.Rd

For each intervention object in interventions_vec, evaluates the entomological model on every day of the intervention and returns the average vectorial capacity and impact (reduction in vectorial capacity) at each coverage. This is run_interventions applied to the parameters stored in each intervention ($param_set), so both functions give the same results and the same output format.

The model parameters are those of model_p (the model_p used to build the interventions does not matter).

Usage

calculate_impact(
  interventions_vec,
  coverage_vec,
  model_p,
  exposure = 1,
  keep_time = FALSE
)

Arguments

interventions_vec

Intervention objects created with build_intervention(), combined with c() (e.g. c(itn1, itn2)); a single build_intervention() output works as is.

coverage_vec

Numeric vector of deployment coverages (values in [0, 1]). The impact is always computed relative to coverage 0 (no intervention), which is evaluated internally when not supplied.

model_p

Model object created with build_model_obj().

exposure

Proportion of human exposure to bites that occurs where the intervention protects, in [0, 1] (default 1). The intervention acts on an effective coverage coverage_vec * exposure. Typically calculate_exposure(...)$Exposure_Indoor_whileinbed for ITNs, and $indoor_resting or $Exposure_Indoor_total for IRS (see calculate_exposure). Reported coverages remain the deployment coverages.

keep_time

Logical (default FALSE): also return the vectorial capacity and impact on each day.

Value

A data.table with one row per intervention and coverage: intervention (position in interventions_vec), name, the intervention parameters (as in run_interventions()), coverage, exposure, avg_vc and avg_impact. With keep_time = TRUE, a list with this table as impact and a long table time with intervention, name, coverage, day (0 = deployment), vc and impact. Plot it with plot_impact.
